content.title: Types: Values Behave Differently
content.hook: Not all values behave the same way. A number, a string, a boolean, and an empty-value marker each mean different things.
content.context: Not all values behave the same way. A number, a string, a boolean, and an empty-value marker each mean different things.
goals: Recognize common JavaScript value types and predict how operations differ by type.

content.title: Four types
content.text:
For this lesson, know these four:

```js
42          // number
"42"       // string
true        // boolean
null        // intentional absence of a value
```

The quotes matter. `42` is a number; `"42"` is text.

content.question:
What is the result of this expression?

```js
"4" + "2"
```

feedback.correct: Both operands are strings, so `+` joins them into the string `"42"`.
feedback.incorrect: Both operands are strings, so `+` joins them into the string `"42"`.

content.title: Compare values
content.text:
```js
5 === 5
5 === "5"
```

The first expression is `true`. The second is `false` because the values are not the same type and value.

For Forge, use `===` when you mean **strict equality**: same value and same type.

content.title: Boolean thinking
content.text:
Booleans have two values: `true` and `false`. They are useful when the program needs to answer a yes/no question.

```js
const hasPaid = true;
```

That name is easy to reason about because the value answers a question.

content.prompt:
Predict both results:

```js
10 + 5
"10" + 5
```


The operator is the same. The values are different. The type changes the result.
guidelines: State your reasoning clearly in your own words or code.
Compare your response with the reference guide after submitting.

options.text: `"5"` and `5` are the same JavaScript value.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: **Mental model:** Ask two questions: **What value is this? What type is it?**
**Senior habit:** Many JavaScript bugs become easier once you stop looking only at the spelling of a value and start checking what kind of value it is.
nextSteps: Complete the checkpoint and explain the mechanism in your own words. A wrong first prediction is expected; the mastery signal is whether you can explain the result and handle a changed case after feedback.
